evidence.title: Firecreek
evidence.text: Firecreek is a 1968 American western film directed by Vincent McEveety and starring James Stewart and Henry Fonda in his second role as an antagonist that year.

evidence.title: Firecreek
evidence.text: The film is similar to" High Noon" in that it features an entire town of cowards refusing to help a peace officer against outlaws.

evidence.title: Firecreek
evidence.text: Stewart plays an unlikely hero, forced into action when his conscience will not permit evil to continue.

evidence.title: Firecreek
evidence.text: Offscreen close friends Stewart and Fonda's first film together had been the musical comedy" On Our Merry Way" two decades earlier, and they made" The Cheyenne Social Club" two years after" Firecreek".

evidence.title: Firecreek
evidence.text: They had also both appeared in" How the West Was Won" but had no scenes together despite playing best friends.

evidence.title: Firecreek
evidence.text: It was partially filmed at North Ranch in Thousand Oaks, California.
